take_homes: Rolling out licences and people using the tool are two different numbers. I will ask for both next time someone reports an AI rollout.
An empty owner field is the real project status. Before any pilot I want one named person accountable.
Ask what the person uses today and what would have to be true for them to drop it. Do not pick a tool because it fits our platform.

monday.move: Take the one finance process where we already hold a licence or tool and ask one person how they actually do that job today. Ask what would have to be true for them to switch. Write the owner's name next to it, or leave it blank.
monday.who: My controller, on month-end variance commentary
monday.when: Wednesday, 15 minutes, after the Monday leadership meeting
monday.stop_condition: If she cannot name what she does today in two sentences, or nobody will own it, I stop and say no for now.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved any AI tool for finance data, and I have no cost per user or payback figure to take to the board.

misconception.why: The 'licence you buy' idea took a hit when it was said that access gets reported as if it were use. That matches the programmes I have seen fail. I still don't know what building the capability costs, and the module never gave me a figure, so I only half believe it.

one_line: Good on why rollouts stall and on the empty owner field, but it assumes you built a system first, and nobody put a number on any of it.
